sentences.text: This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by the appellant/plaintiff against rejection of I.A.No.1 filed under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 of CPC, wherein prayed the relief of temporary injunction restraining the defendants or anybody on their behalf from interfering with plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment over the suit 'A' and 'B' schedule properties.
3. The plaintiff also sought for a judgment and decree declaring that the plaintiff is the lawful and absolute owner in possession of the suit schedule properties and so also permanent injunction.

Consequently, the plaintiff also sought for the relief that gift deed dated 01.10.2011 is not binding upon the plaintiff and so also for a judgment and decree declaring that registered sale deed dated 07.07.2017 executed by defendant No.1 along with her family members through her GPA holder in favour of Smt. B. Jayanthi is not binding upon the plaintiff and also sought to declare that the registered sale deed dated 07.07.2017 executed in favour of Murali is not binding on the plaintiff and such other relief.
The plaintiff also filed an application for temporary injunction restraining the defendants from interfering with peaceful possession over the suit schedule properties.

4. The factual matrix of the case of the plaintiff through GPA holder is that suit 'A' and 'B' schedule properties were purchased by the plaintiff vide registered sale deeds dated 17.03.2023 and 01.04.2023 from one Shilpa Niranjan Shetty and Shruthi Hegde respectively.

It is contended that suit 'A' schedule property was allotted to mother of the vendor of the plaintiff by name Sumathi A.
Hegde and the same was registered in the name of Sumathi A. Hegde on 04.04.2009 .

The said Sumathi A. Hegde had executed gift deed in respect of 'A' schedule property in favour of the vendor of the plaintiff by name Shilpa Niranjan Shetty vide registered gift deed dated 12.04.2022.

The said Shilpa Niranjan Shetty sold suit 'A' schedule property in favour of the plaintiff vide registered sale deed dated 17.03.2023.
5.

It is also contended that suit 'B' schedule property was allotted to Shruthi Hegde and the same was registered in her name vide sale deed dated 04.04.2009 and the said Shruthi Hegde sold suit 'B'
schedule property in favour of the plaintiff vide registered sale deed dated 01.04.2023.
It is further contended that prior to sale deed in favour of the plaintiff, khatha in respect of the suit schedule properties was standing in the name of his vendors with the BBMP.
The plaintiff is in possession of the suit schedule properties from the date of registered sale deeds itself and is enjoying possession of the said properties.
The defendants are claiming themselves as the owners of the suit schedule properties and are interfering with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties by the plaintiff.
Hence, the plaintiff has approached the jurisdictional police station, but he was advised to approach the Civil Court as the dispute is civil in nature.

6. It is further contended by the plaintiff that by virtue of the order of the Apex Court as well as observation made by this Court in the writ proceedings before the respective Courts, the property in Sy.No.34/1 of Nagawara Village was sold by the land owners in favour of one Kariyappa.

Kariyappa along with M/s. Vyalikaval House Building Co-operative Society Ltd. had formed layout and suit 'A'
and 'B' schedule properties were formed in Sy.No.34/1 of Nagawara Village.

The Trial Court while passing the impugned order in paragraph No.42 discussed the pleadings of the parties and taken note of the fact that property was restored in the name of original owner.

The Trial Court also taken note of the case of the plaintiff regarding sale deed dated 04.04.2009 executed by M/s.

The Trial Court also taken note of the fact that as per the schedule in both the sale deeds, several survey numbers are mentioned.

Hence, comes to the conclusion that suit schedule properties comes within Sy.No.34/1 cannot be identified and the matter requires full-fledged trial and plaintiff has not made out prima facie case and rejected the application.
Being aggrieved by the order of the Trial Court on I.A.No.1 in O.S.No.7281/2023, the present miscellaneous second appeal is filed before this Court.

14. The main contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the finding of the Trial Court is erroneous in coming to the conclusion that the plaintiff has not made out a prima facie case.

The Trial Court has failed to take note of the fact that title flows in favour of the plaintiff through the registered documents and all the documents issued by the BDA and subsequently issued by BBMP stands in the name of the plaintiff and that itself is a prima facie material to show that the plaintiff is the owner in possession of the property.

Learned counsel also would vehemently contend that Trial Court has grossly erred in failing to appreciate that this Court in identical matter pertaining to the very same respondents/defendants in respect of very same layout and land in Sy.No.34/1 as regards site Nos.411 and 416 has granted an order of temporary injunction by order dated 23.04.2018 in M.F.A.No.2433/2018 and the same has also been confirmed by the Apex Court.
The order of temporary injunction is still operating against the very same defendants.
Though the same has been placed before the Trial Court, the Trial Court has failed to consider the same.
15. Learned counsel also brought to notice of this Court the said order which is produced before this Court along with the appeal memo at Page No.136.

Learned counsel would vehemently contend that the Trial Court failed to take note of the fact that plaintiff has failed to establish that he is in possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties.

The Possession Certificate of the predecessors-in-title, registered sale deeds, khatha certificates issued by BDA and BBMP would conclusively prove that the appellant/plaintiff is in possession of the suit schedule properties.

The Trial Court also failed to consider the fact that 1 acre 8 guntas of land had been sold by the children of original land owners under registered sale deeds dated 20.05.2003 to Kariyappa, who in turn had got converted the land for residential purpose and thereafter, M/s. Thus, the defendant No.1 or her grand-mother never had any right, title or interest in execution of the gift deed, since none of them had title to the property in question and this fact has not been considered by the Trial Court and it requires interference of this Court.
16. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3 would vehemently contend that very sale in favour of Kariyappa itself is in dispute.
Learned counsel would vehemently contend that identity of the property is also disputed whether it comes within Sy.No.34/1 of Nagawara Village.
The Trial Court while rejecting the application has given reasons with regard to the dispute in respect of title and the matter requires full-fledged trial.
The Trial Court has also given definite finding with regard to identity of the property.

17. The counsel also relied upon the judgment of this Court in MALAR VENI VS. RAMAMURTHY reported in AIR 2023 KARNATAKA 302, wherein this Court confirmed the order of rejection of interim order and comes to the conclusion that when the very possession, identity and title is in dispute, the question of granting an order of temporary injunction that plaintiff has made out a prima facie case does not arise and the said judgment is aptly applicable to the case on hand.
18.

sentences.text: In reply to the argument of the learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3, learned counsel for the appellant brought notice of this Court detailed discussion made by this Court in the appeal in M.F.A.No.2433/2018, wherein also defendant No.1 was a party.

This Court observed that every observation in the course of this order is not an expression of opinion on merits, but is only for the limited purposes of deciding the appeal and that the appellant's every use of the suit schedule properties shall be subject to the peril of the final adjudication in the suit without the appellant being entitled to claim any equity, and that the appellant being liable to answer any substantiated claim by the respondent for the losses, if any, as a consequence of the suit being finally adjudicated against the appellant.
Hence, this Court has to grant the relief of temporary injunction in the light of the observations made by this Court.
The respective counsels have also produced documents which have been produced before the Trial Court and brought the same to the notice of this Court.

19. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellant, learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3 and also considering the grounds which have been urged and also the documents which are produced before this Court, the points that would arise for consideration of this Court are:
(1) Whether the Trial Court has committed an error in dismissing the application filed under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 of CPC and it requires interference of this Court?
(2) What order?
Point No.(1)
20.
The specific case of the plaintiff in this appeal is that the original owners have executed a sale deed in favour of one Kariyappa in the year 2003.

He had got converted the property on behalf of M/s. Vyalikaval House Building Co-operative Society Ltd. and the said Society has formed layout Sri. K Y Sivasankara Reddy vs Smt. Munirathnamma on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136289121/

The Trial Court also in paragraph No.44 made an observation that the sale deeds executed by M/s. sentences.text: But, the Trial Court comes to the conclusion that the identity of the property is in dispute.
The said observation made by the Trial Court is erroneous and comes to the conclusion that plaintiff has not made out a prima facie case and it requires full-fledged trial.

It has to be noted that, the suit is filed for declaration to declare the plaintiff as the owner and also sought to declare that subsequent sale deeds executed are not binding on the plaintiff as the documents which have been executed by the executants i.e., gift deed dated 01.10.2011 and sale deeds dated 07.07.2017 are not binding.

Since the property had already been sold, execution of gift deed or any other sale deed are not binding on the plaintiff and the Trial Court ought to have taken note of the said fact into consideration and it was not stated before the Trial Court that property was not sold in favour of Kariyappa, since already there was prima facie material to substantiate the fact that an extent of 1 acre 8 guntas was sold in favour of Kariyappa and the sale deed executed in respect of the said property is also not in dispute.

22. Though the said sale deed is disputed that the same is void, no relief is sought questioning the sale deed in any proceedings and the only contention is that vendors are not having any right to execute sale deed in respect of Sy.No.34/1.
When the defendants are also claiming right in respect of Sy.No.34/1, the sale deed of the year 2003 was not challenged and nothing is placed on record before the Court.

When such being the case, the plaintiff has made out a prima facie case stating that there were two sale deeds in favour of Kariyappa to an extent of 1 acre 8 guntas and the title and Sri. who is brother of Appoji @ Appajappa and the fact that Appoji @ Appajappa is the original owner of the land bearing Sy.No.34/1 and that he had three sons by name Krishnappa, Narayanappa and Muniyappa is not in dispute.

Venkatamma, who had executed the gift deed dated 01.10.2011 is the wife of Krishnappa and her husband was also a party to sale deed in favour of Kariyappa and all of them have sold the property in favour of Kariyappa, including the grand-son.
23.

When such being the case, when the said sale deeds have not been questioned, the Trial Court ought not to have come to the conclusion that there is no prima facie case and the very approach of the Trial Court is erroneous.

When prima facie material is placed by the plaintiff before the Court that there was sale deed dated 20.05.2003 and subsequently, sites are allotted by the Society and in turn, the allottees have sold the properties and sale deeds are executed in favour of the plaintiff,
ultimately, the plaintiff claims as the owner of the suit schedule properties and the documents of BDA and BBMP stands in the name of the plaintiff, the Trial Court ought not to have come to the conclusion that there is no prima facie case.

The material on record also disclose regarding delivery of possession by executing the document of registered sale deed and when the documents stands in the name of plaintiff, balance of convenience and hardship lies in favour of the appellant/plaintiff and the Trial Court failed to consider the same and ought to have discussed other two cardinal principles of granting temporary injunction regarding balance of convenience and hardship.

24. It is also important to note that, in similar set of facts and circumstances, this Court against the very same defendants i.e., defendant No.1 passed an order on 23.04.2018 in M.F.A.No.2433/2018 in respect of very same survey number and granted an order of injunction.

However, made an observation by setting aside the order of the Trial Court and restrained the respondent therein from interfering with the appellant's possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties pending disposal of the suit.

This Court also observed that every observation in the course of this order is not an expression of opinion on merits, but is only for the limited purposes of deciding the appeal and that the appellant's every use of the suit schedule properties shall be subject to the peril of the final adjudication in the suit without the appellant being entitled to claim any equity, and that the appellant being liable to answer any substantiated claim by the respondent for the losses, if any, as a consequence of the suit being finally adjudicated against the appellant.
When this order was brought to notice of the Court, the Trial Court failed to take note of the said fact into consideration.
When such being the case, in view of the observation made by this Court in M.F.A.No.2433/2018, the plaintiff is also entitled for the similar relief considering the facts of the case on hand.
Hence, the order of the Trial Court requires to be set aside by allowing this appeal.
Accordingly, I answer point No.(1) in the 'affirmative'.
Point No.(2)

25. In view of the discussion made above, I pass the following:

When the defendants are also claiming right in respect of Sy.No.34/1, the sale deed of the year 2003 was not challenged and nothing is placed on record before the Court.
property was transferred and right had vested with Kariyappa and the vendor Krishnappa is none other than the son of Appoji @ Appajappa and Venkatesh is none other than the son of Muniyappa,
who is brother of Appoji @ Appajappa and the fact that Appoji @ Appajappa is the original owner of the land bearing Sy.No.34/1 and that he had three sons by name Krishnappa, Narayanappa and Muniyappa is not in dispute.
